.ad-wrapper[data-astro-cid-fgwukgf6]{margin:2rem 0;text-align:center} Air Fryer Toolkit Convert Reverse Food presets Brands Chart Guide EN English Español Português Français Deutsch Time by size Same temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Pack says Shoestring or skinny fries 400°F / 205°C · 11 min 425°F / 220°C · 15 min Regular straight-cut fries 400°F / 205°C · 15 min 425°F / 220°C · 21 min Steak fries or thick-cut chips 400°F / 205°C · 19 min 425°F / 220°C · 26 min Why frozen fries come out soggy Every frozen fry carries a thin glaze of ice, and in the first few minutes that ice melts and turns to steam. With room around each piece the steam blows away and the surface browns in the oil the factory already fried them in. Tip in the whole bag and the steam is trapped: the bottom fries sit in their own water and come out pale and limp however long you leave them. Fill the basket no more than halfway and cook a big bag in two rounds. The 2 shakes do the rest, breaking up fries that froze together and turning the damp bottom layer up into the airflow. Worked example: turning the bag into an air fryer setting A typical bag of straight-cut fries says 425°F for 21 minutes in the oven. A basket air fryer cannot go that hot, so it runs at 400°F and the time drops to 15 minutes, because the fan moves heat into the fries much faster than a tray does. Preheat for 4 minutes, add half the bag, and shake at roughly a third and two thirds of the way through. Shoestring fries are ready in about 11 minutes; steak fries need about 19. A UK bag printed for a fan oven reads 400°F (205°C) for 21 minutes and lands on the same air fryer setting. How to tell they are done Frozen fries are already cooked, so you are after colour and crunch. Snap one: the outside should be golden and crackle, the inside fluffy and hot. If the bottom of the basket is still pale, give it one more shake and two more minutes. Thicker cuts look done before the centre is soft, so taste a steak fry before you pull the batch. Before they go in Do not thaw them, and break up frozen clumps before tipping them in. Oil is optional because the fries were par-fried, though a quick spray helps crinkle-cut fries brown evenly. Salt after cooking, not before, so the salt does not draw out more water. About 15 minutes at 400°F for regular fries, shaken 2 times. Shoestring fries take about 11 minutes and steak fries about 19. Should I thaw frozen fries before air frying? No. Cook them straight from the freezer. Thawing lets the surface go wet and soft, and they never crisp properly afterwards. Do frozen fries need oil in the air fryer? Not usually. They were par-fried before freezing, so they brown on their own. A light spray helps seasoned or crinkle-cut fries colour more evenly. Why are my frozen fries still soggy? Too many in the basket. The ice on each fry turns to steam, and a full basket traps it. Cook half a bag at a time and shake as the timer suggests. My bag says 425°F for 21 minutes. What do I set? 400°F for about 15 minutes in a basket air fryer. The converter on this page takes any bag’s numbers, including fan-oven ones. mainEntity.name: How long do frozen fries take in the air fryer?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 15 minutes at 400°F for regular fries, shaken 2 times. Shoestring fries take about 11 minutes and steak fries about 19.

mainEntity.name: Should I thaw frozen fries before air frying?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Cook them straight from the freezer. Thawing lets the surface go wet and soft, and they never crisp properly afterwards.

mainEntity.name: Do frozen fries need oil in the air fryer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not usually. They were par-fried before freezing, so they brown on their own. A light spray helps seasoned or crinkle-cut fries colour more evenly.

mainEntity.name: Why are my frozen fries still soggy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Too many in the basket. The ice on each fry turns to steam, and a full basket traps it. Cook half a bag at a time and shake as the timer suggests.

mainEntity.name: My bag says 425°F for 21 minutes. What do I set?

acceptedAnswer.text: 400°F for about 15 minutes in a basket air fryer. The converter on this page takes any bag’s numbers, including fan-oven ones.
